list.name: fn
list.description: Function label domain is closed at image-build time by the demuxer's boot-time allowlist (charts/pawtograder/images/edge-functions/main.ts); anything off that list reports as "_unknown".

list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Backed by the PROMETHEUS datasource, deliberately. This variable is interpolated into kube-state-metrics and cAdvisor expressions; it used to be a Loki label_values query, which worked only because both label sets happen to contain the same namespace string. Scoping Loki log collection down would have emptied the value list and blanked every Prometheus panel here for a reason unrelated to Prometheus. The regex bounds All to pawtograder-* namespaces, and exactly one exists per environment, so All resolves correctly in every environment.

panels.title: P95 latency
panels.description: POD-WIDE, across all functions: pawtograder_edge_request_duration_seconds has no function label, so the $fn selector is deliberately absent here — adding it would match nothing and the panel would go blank. Per-function latency is the panel below, as a mean. This measures TIME TO HEADERS, not full response time: the demuxer sees the response when headers are ready and a streaming body finishes later.

panels.title: User workers active
panels.description: Live user-worker isolates across the fleet, from EdgeRuntime.getRuntimeMetrics() on each pod's main worker.

panels.title: Mean latency by function
panels.description:
Mean time-to-headers per function, and the share of total demuxer time each function accounts for. NOT quantiles: pawtograder_edge_request_duration_seconds is pod-wide and carries no function label. DECIDED 2026-09-03 — adding that label takes the edge tier from ~8.6k to ~37k series, every one of them per-pod, so an HPA excursion to 64 replicas doubles the count at exactly the moment of load. If someone later adds the label deliberately, these are the expressions this panel used to carry:

  histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by(le, function)(rate(pawtograder_edge_request_duration_seconds_bucket{function=~"$fn"}[5m])))
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le, function)(rate(pawtograder_edge_request_duration_seconds_bucket{function=~"$fn"}[5m])))
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by(le, function)(rate(pawtograder_edge_request_duration_seconds_bucket{function=~"$fn"}[5m])))

panels.title: Worker retirements & demuxer errors
panels.description: Retirements are NORMAL: the runtime recycles an isolate as it approaches its memory, CPU-time or wall-clock limit, and a healthy fleet retires constantly. The errors are the signal. retired_retry means a request landed on an about-to-die worker and was retried on a fresh one (recovered, but a sustained rise means isolates are being retired faster than they are used). cancelled means the supervisor killed a worker mid-request and the caller got a 503. internal is everything else, and is always worth reading the logs for.

panels.title: Pod restarts (30m)
panels.description: A restart here kills PID 1, so every in-flight request on that pod dies at once and Kong returns 502 to the caller — including the grading runner. Spikes here line up with 502 spikes to the second.

panels.title: Memory vs limit
panels.description: Fraction of the container memory limit. The OOM kill follows this crossing 1.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", container="functions"} / on(namespace, pod, container) kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace=~"$namespace", container="functions", resource="memory"})

panels.title: OOMKilled terminations
panels.description: 1 while a pod's last termination reason was OOMKilled.

panels.title: Working set memory vs pod age
panels.description: Decomposes the container working set. eszip cache is the demuxer's resident bundle LRU; main heap is the pod-lifetime main isolate. Working set minus those two is user-worker isolates plus the Deno host. container_memory_working_set_bytes alone cannot separate the three, which is why the 2026-08-19 cache leak looked like generic memory growth for days.

panels.title: Logs — $namespace / $fn
panels.description: Edge-function stdout from Loki, filtered to the selected function(s) via the [fn=<name>] tag stamped by the demuxer (main.ts) and wrapRequestHandler. Pick a single $fn to isolate one function.
